vulnerability: Missing allowance check in transferFrom allows arbitrary token theft
reason: transferFrom never checks or consumes allowance for sender. Any external account can call it with an arbitrary sender and recipient. After canTrade is true, _transfer only enforces blacklist and lock checks, and the lock check uses the victim's balance, so an attacker can steal any unlocked NOVO, including the staking pool. Even before trading, if sender is the owner, _tokenTransfer only requires sender == owner(), so anyone can call transferFrom(owner, attacker, amount) and drain the owner's balance. This is a direct theft vulnerability.

vulnerability: Repeated reward calculation drains staking pool
reason: getReward computes rewards from novo.balanceOf(address(this)) / 2, where address(this) is the NovoNFT contract, but it never reduces that balance or deducts already-paid rewards. It only adds the computed rewards to mapStakers and totalBagSize. NOVO.transfer and NOVO.transferFrom call getReward whenever the recipient is the router and then pay the returned amount from _stakingPoolAddress. An attacker with a stake can repeatedly trigger this by transferring a tiny amount to the router. The time-based component is additive and uses the same elapsed time and same NFT-contract balance each call, so repeated calls can drain the staking pool. Early-unstaking fees or donations to the NFT contract make the reward even larger.

vulnerability: Transferable stake NFT can lock arbitrary address and freeze liquidity
reason: transfer enforces the lock using getLockedAmount(msg.sender), which sums mapStakers for all NFTs currently owned by msg.sender. Since the ERC721 stake NFT is freely transferable and mapStakers is tied to the tokenId, not the original staker, transferring an NFT moves the entire recorded principal and reward lock to the recipient. An attacker can mint one NFT with a large _stakingAmount, transfer it to the Uniswap pair or any victim, and thereby set that address's locked amount to a large value. The pair cannot call unstaking, so its NOVO transfers will be permanently blocked or severely restricted because balanceOf(pair) - amount must remain greater than or equal to lockedAmount. The attacker's own NOVO becomes unlocked after the NFT transfer, so the attack is cheap and can freeze liquidity.
